 Judgment

This petition is filed by the petitioner U/s.166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest from the date of petition till its realization for injuries sustained by him in the Motor Vehicle Accident.

2. The brief case of the petitioner is as under:
On 29-07-2023 at about 1.30 p.m., when the petitioner was going on the motor cycle bearing reg.No.KA- (SCCH-9) 3 MVC.No.7276/2023 51-Y-2566 on the left side of Bengaluru-Tumkur NH 48 road, Binnamangala, near Reliance petrol bunk, Nelamangala, at that time, driver of the Swift car bearing reg.No.KA-02-MU-1977 came with high speed from his behind in a rash and negligent manner, after overtaking petitioner's motor cycle, car driver abruptly without giving any signal, came towards left side of the road and dashed against the petitioner's motor cycle, due to impact, petitioner and pillion rider thrown on the road and sustained severe injuries.

Immediately after the accident, petitioner was shifted to Nelamangala Govt., Hospital wherein first aid was done, then he was shifted to Sanjay Gandhi hospital, Bengaluru wherein the petitioner was treated as inpatient and undergone operation.
Prior to the accident, petitioner was doing Bar bender work running Onion business with transport business and earning monthly Rs.30,000/- per month.
Due to said (SCCH-9) 4 MVC.No.7276/2023 accident, he lost his future income.
The Nelamangala Traffic police have registered a criminal case against the driver of the Swift car bearing No.KA-02-MU-1977 in crime No.322/2023 under Section 279 and 338 of IPC.
The respondent No.2 being the RC owner and respondent No.1 being the insurer are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
3. After service of summons, the respondent No.2 has not appeared before the court hence, placed exparte and respondent No.1 has appeared before the tribunal and filed its written statement.
4. The brief contents of written statement of respondent No.1 is that, the claim petition is not maintainable in law or on facts.
It has admitted the issuance of the policy in favour of the respondent No.2.
Respondent No.1 has denied the involvement of the car bearing reg.No.KA-02-MU-1977 in the alleged accident.
It has denied the age, occupation, income and amount spent (SCCH-9) 5 MVC.No.7276/2023 by the petitioner.

Further deposed that, the owner of the vehicle did not report and furnished the RTO documents pertaining to the offending vehicle regarding the driving licence of the person who was driving the vehicle at the time of accident which required under Section 134(C) and the concerned police have not complied the mandatory provisions of Sec.159 of MV Act.

It has contented that, at the time of accident, petitioner was riding Kempegowda vs Bajaj All Gen Ins Co Ltd on 5 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18928213/
2 his vehicle without holding valid and effective driving licence and also without observing the movements of the vehicles.

The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive, (SCCH-9) 6 MVC.No.7276/2023 exorbitant and exaggerated.
With these grounds the respondent No.1 sought for rejecting the claim petition.

5. On the basis of above pleadings, this Tribunal has framed the following issues:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner prove that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 29-07-2023 at about 1.30 p.m. on Bengaluru-Tumkur NH-48 road, Binnamangala, near reliance petrol bunk, Nelamangala, Bengaluru due to rash and negligent act of driving of Car bearing registration No.KA-02-MU-1977 by its driver as alleged in the petition?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, to what amount and from whom?
3. What Order or Award?
6.

Orthopaedic surgeon and also Professor Orthopaedics at Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma and orthopaedics, Bangalore has examined as PW.2 and in all got marked (SCCH-9) 7 MVC.No.7276/2023 documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P.16.

On perusal of police documents which are (SCCH-9) 9 MVC.No.7276/2023 marked at Ex-P1 to Ex-P6 it is clear that the accident took place on 29-07-2023 at about 1.30 p.m., and Ex.
P.1 - FIR in crime No.0322/2023 came to be registered on 29-07- 2023 at about 1.30 p.m. i.e., on the same of accident at Nelamangala Police Station for the offences punishable u/s 279, 337 of IPC.
Ex.P.2 - complaint lodged by Appajigowda S/o Kempegowda/petitioner on 29-07-2023.

Ex.P.3 is the panchanama, Ex.P4 is the MVA report, Ex.P5 is the wound certificate, Ex.P6 is the charge sheet which describe the spot of accident as towards Nelamangala Taluk, Kasaba hobli, Binnamangala reliance petrol bunk, Bangalore-Tumkur NH 48 road and Ex.P.7 and 8 are the discharge summaries,

Ex.P9 is the 12 OPD, Ex.P.4 is the IMV report which shows the damages caused the vehicles which involved in the alleged accident I.e., motor cycle bearing No.KA-51-Y-2566 and car bearing No.KA-02-MU- 1977.
Ex.P.6 is the charge sheet which has been filed against the driver of car bearing No.KA-02-MU-1977.
. The learned counsel for the respondent No.1 has cross examined PW-1.
I have perused the entire cross- examination of PW-1.

In his cross-examination he has specifically denied the suggestions made by the learned counsel for the respondent regarding negligence of driver of car bearing No.KA-02-MU-1977, the alleged accident occurred.
The learned counsel for the respondent No.1 has not elicited anything from the mouth of PW-1 to disbelieve his version.
There is nothing on record to show that the charge-sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.

Therefore, on over all appreciation of evidence, I am of the opinion that the accident occurred due to sole negligence of driver of the offending car bearing registration No.KA- 02-MU-1977 which belongs to the respondent No.2 and respondent No.1 is its insurer.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
14. Issue No.2: In view of answering Issue No.1 in the affirmative the petitioner is entitled for compensation.

To assess the compensation, the Tribunal has to look into several facts like injuries, pain and suffering, sustained by the petitioner and amount spent by the petitioner towards medical expenses, food and extra nourishment, medical and attendant charges, conveyance,
loss of income during treatment, disability, loss of amenities etc. let me discuss one by one:
a) Towards Injury, Pain and Suffering: The petitioner has contended due to accident he has sustained grievous injury i.e., swelling in left thigh fracture, left femur shaft fracture.

In order to prove injuries caused to him, he has produced wound certificate marked at Ex.P.5 issued by Government Hospital, Nelamangala which reveals that petitioner has sustained swelling in left thigh fracture femur and left femur fracture shaft and doctor has opined that injury is grievous in nature.
Further, Petitioner examined Dr.Chidanand K.J.C. and got marked OPD record, case sheet and X-rays marked at (SCCH-9) 12 MVC.No.7276/2023 Ex.P.14 to Ex.P.16.
PW.2 has assessed the disability of petitioner.
Therefore by considering the injury and facts and circumstances of the case the Tribunal is of the view that the compensation of Rs.50,000/- is just and reasonable towards pain and sufferings.
b) Towards Medical Expenses:
Petitioner has produced 32 medical bills for a sum of Rs.96,288/- which are marked at Ex.P.11.

During cross examination of Pw.1,
Respondent No.1 has not put any suggestion therefore, it has been considered that,
those medical bills are genuine and correct.
Therefore it is just and reasonable to award Rs.96,288/- under the head medical expenses.

c) Towards food, extra nourishment, Conveyance and medical attendant charges:
PW.1 has deposed that, immediately after accident he took treatment as an inpatient at Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma and orthopaedics.

sentences.text: As per discharge summary marked at Ex.P.7 which discloses that, petitioner took (SCCH-9) 13 MVC.No.7276/2023 treatment at Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma and orthopaedics from 29-7-2023 to 10-08-2023 i.e., for 13 days.
Further petitioner took treatment as inpatient at Prerana health care from 5-1-2024 to 6-1-2024 for two days.

Considering the said fact the Tribunal is of the view that compensation of Rs.1,000/-
per day for 15 days and by including conveyance, in all a sum of Rs.15,000/- is just and reasonable towards food extra nourishment, conveyance and medical attendant charges.
d) Towards Loss of Income during treatment:
The petitioner contended that he was working as Bar bender and earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
The petitioner has not produced any document to prove his avocation and income.

So in view of fixing of notional income by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, it is just and proper to this Tribunal to follow the notional income as fixed by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka to decide the cases before this Tribunal also.

Accordingly, the fixed notional (SCCH-9) 14 MVC.No.7276/2023 income of the year 2023 at 16,000/- p.m., Petitioner may took 3 months rest and he Kempegowda vs Bajaj All Gen Ins Co Ltd on 5 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18928213/
5 may lost income for those rest periods.

Therefore, by considering the facts and circumstances of the case the petitioner is entitled to Rs.48,000/- (Rs.16,000/- x 3)
towards loss of income during treatment period.
e) Towards Future Earnings:
The petitioner has contended that due to accident he took treatment as an inpatient in the hospital and has become permanently disabled.

The petitioner has also examined Dr.Chidanand K.J.C. working as Orthopaedic surgeon and professor orthopaedics at Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma and orthopaedics, Bangalore-11 as PW.2 and contended that, he has examined a patient by name Kempegowda on 29-7- 2023 with history of RTA and petitioner has sustained injuries i.e., left femur shaft fracture type 2 open, petitioner underwent surgery in the form of CRIF with IMIL nailing and was discharged on 10-8-2023. PW-2 (SCCH-9) 15 MVC.No.7276/2023 further stated that 5-3-2025 petitioner came for disability assessment and following points noted i.e., range of movements of knee, hip restricted,
quadricepts wasting is seen, painful hip and knee joint line, associated with pain on movements knee hip, daily activities cross leg sitting, squatting for using, Indian toilets were found to be difficulty in limb, x-ray femur shows fracture united with implant in situ.

sentences.text: PW.2 assessed permanent physical disability for limb is 45% and to the wholebody at 15%.
During cross examination PW.2 has admitted that he has not done surgery to the petitioner.
It is relevant to note that according to PW.2 has assessed permanent physical disability for limb is 45% and to the wholebody at 15%.

It is well settled law that it is the impact of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court (SCCH-9)
16 MVC.No.7276/2023 in Rajkumar's case reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343.
By looking into the record it seems that PW.2 has assessed disability of the Petitioner at higher side.
Therefore, the Petitioner might be having 13% disability to the whole body which cannot be ruled out.
The petitioner has produced Ex.P.10 - Aadhar card in order to prove his age.

As per said document,
he was born on 03-03-1963 and as on date of accident he was aged about 60 years.

Under such circumstances, the age of petitioner was considered as 60 years and same is taken into consideration for applying multiplier and the proper multiplier is "09" is applicable as per Smt.Sarala Verma's case.

Hence future earning capacity of the petitioner due to permanent disability works out as under:
16,000 x 12 x 09 x 13% = Rs.2,24,640/- Therefore, the petitioner is entitled Rs.2,24,640/- under the head of loss of future earning capacity.

Regarding Liability:

The respondent No.1 has taken contention that, at the time of accident,
petitioner was riding his vehicle without holding valid and effective (SCCH-9) 19 MVC.No.7276/2023 driving licence.
In this regard perused the record, petitioner has produced the Ex-P12-driving licence.
PW-1 during his cross-examination clearly deposed that Ex-P12 is his driving licence, it is not denied by the respondent.
Hence, there is no reason to believe the defence of the respondent that at the time of accident, petitioner has not holding valid and effective driving licence.
17. Further the respondent No.1 has taken another defence that petitioner was riding the vehicle without observing the movements of the vehicles.

In this regard, perused the petition wherein submitted that Swift car bearing reg.No.KA-02-MU-1977 came with high speed from his behind in a rash and negligent manner, after overtaking petitioner's motor cycle, car driver abruptly without giving any signal, he came towards left side of the road and dashed against the petitioner's motor Kempegowda vs Bajaj All Gen Ins Co Ltd on 5 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18928213/
7 cycle.

sentences.text: Further after investigation, IO has filed final report as per Ex-P6 in support of the petitioner.

PW-1 subjected to cross- (SCCH-9) 20 MVC.No.7276/2023 examination wherein he clearly deposed that Swift car came in a rash and negligent manner immediately while over taking he dashed to the petitioner's motor cycle,
due to which accident occurred
. Further PW-1 clearly denied the suggestion that due to his rash and negligent driving accident occurred.
Hence except the suggestion, respondent No.1 has not produced any documentary evidence to prove his defence.
Hence the defence of the respondent No.1 is not believable that due to the negligence of the petitioner, accident occurred.

18. Further in support of his defence, the learned counsel for the respondent No.1 relied upon the citation reported in AIR-2018-SC-2118 between -Nishanth Singh Vs Oriental insurance company Ltd., wherein Hon'ble Supreme Court held that- 23.

entities.text: -Nishanth Singh Vs Oriental insurance company Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Distance from vehicles in front.

The driver of a motor vehicle moving behind another vehicle shall keep at a sufficient distance from that other vehicle to avoid collusion if the vehicle in front should (SCCH-9) 21 MVC.No.7276/2023 suddenly show down or stop.
The expression 'sufficient distance' has not been defined in the regulations or elsewhere.
The thumb rule of sufficient distance is at least a safe distance of two to three seconds gap in ideal conditions to avert collision and to allow the following driver time to respond.
The distance of 10-15 feet between the truck and maruti car was certainly not a safe distance for which the driver of the maruti car must take the blame.
It must necessarily follow that the finding on the issue under consideration ought to be against the claimants.

19. In the above decision, the driver of the truck suddenly applied the break while the truck was in the centre of the road, bringing it to the right side, as a result of which, the Maruti car colluded with the truck from the back, due to which accident occurred, but in the present case, while overtaking the motor cycle, driver of the Swift car dashed to the petitioner's motor cycle, due to which accident occurred.
Hence the above citation is not applicable to the case on hand.
Further respondent No.1 has taken defence that petitioner was not wearing helmet at the time of alleged accident.
Petitioner was riding his two wheeler in zigzag manner and he himself has fell from the two wheeler and sustained injuries.
It is clearly denied by the petitioner.
PW-1 subjected to cross examination wherein learned counsel for the respondent No.1 has not put a single suggestion/question about the said defence.
Hence, mere defence taken in the written statement is not sufficient to prove the same in the absence of documentary evidence.

At this juncture, this tribunal relied upon the decision reported in - MFA No.3459/2021(MV-1) ( Sri. Sadath Ali Khan Va.
Sri. Noor Ahmed Sayeed and another) wherein it is held that - " 26.
However, not wearing protective headgear does not negate the right to compensation.

Courts have consistently held that the compensation awarded should not be diluted solely because the (SCCH-9) 23 MVC.No.7276/2023 injured party was Kempegowda vs Bajaj All Gen Ins Co Ltd on 5 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18928213/
8 not wearing protective headgear.

sentences.text: The principle of "just compensation" requires that while contributory negligence can be a factor in determining the amount of compensation, it should not result in an unjust reduction.
The compensation must be fair and reasonable, reflecting the actual losses and the nature of injuries sustained.

NC: 2024:KHC:28807-DB had come to the conclusion that the claimant cannot take shelter under the cited case laws as there is a violation of Section 129 of the Act in not wearing the helmet at the relevant time.
However, the contentious contention is taken by the Insurance Company that the claimant was not wearing the helmet.
But the Motor Vehicles Act is a beneficial legislation.

Keeping in view of the scope of Section 129 of the Act and in a given peculiar facts and circumstances of the case, the entire liability shall be fastened on respondent No.2-insurance company".
21.
By considering the above said citation, at the present case also, not wearing protective headgear does not negate the right to compensation.

22. Therefore, the respondent No.2 being the (SCCH-9) 24 MVC.No.7276/2023 R.C.Owner and the respondent No.1 being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
However, the respondent No.1 being the insurer of offending vehicle is primarily liable to pay compensation with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 answered Partly in the Affirmative.
23. Issue No.3:

In view of the findings given on the above said issues, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The claim petition filed by the petitioner Under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of .4,68,928/- (Rupees four lakhs sixty eight thousand nine hundred and twenty eight only) with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realization.
(future medical expenses shall not carry any interest).
(SCCH-9) 25 MVC.No.7276/2023 Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Respondent No.1 being the insurer is primarily liable to deposit the said compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.

In the event of deposit of the said compensation amount, 25% shall be deposited in the name of petitioner for a period of 3 years in Karnataka Bank, City Civil Court Branch, Bengaluru and the remaining 75% shall be released in favour of petitioner on proper identification through E-payment.
Advocate fee is fixed at .1,000/-.
Draw up award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.facts:
This petition is filed by the petitioner U/s.166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest from the date of petition till its realization for injuries sustained by him in the Motor Vehicle Accident.
The Nelamangala Traffic police have registered a criminal case against the driver of the Swift car bearing No.KA-02-MU-1977 in crime No.322/2023 under Section 279 and 338 of IPC.
The respondent No.2 being the RC owner and respondent No.1 being the insurer are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Petitioner was riding his two wheeler in zigzag manner and he himself has fell from the two wheeler and sustained injuries.
opennyai_summary.issue:
Whether the petitioner prove that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 29-07-2023 at about 1.30 p.m. on Bengaluru-Tumkur NH-48 road, Binnamangala, near reliance petrol bunk, Nelamangala, Bengaluru due to rash and negligent act of driving of Car bearing registration No.KA-02-MU-1977 by its driver as alleged in the petition?

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The petitioner contended that he was working as Bar bender and earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
It is well settled law that it is the impact of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court (SCCH-9)
16 MVC.No.7276/2023 in Rajkumar's case reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343.
By looking into the record it seems that PW.2 has assessed disability of the Petitioner at higher side.
Therefore, the Petitioner might be having 13% disability to the whole body which cannot be ruled out.
Kempegowda vs Bajaj All Gen Ins Co Ltd on 5 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18928213/
Hence the defence of the respondent No.1 is not believable that due to the negligence of the petitioner, accident occurred.
The driver of a motor vehicle moving behind another vehicle shall keep at a sufficient distance from that other vehicle to avoid collusion if the vehicle in front should (SCCH-9) 21 MVC.No.7276/2023 suddenly show down or stop.
The expression 'sufficient distance' has not been defined in the regulations or elsewhere.
The thumb rule of sufficient distance is at least a safe distance of two to three seconds gap in ideal conditions to avert collision and to allow the following driver time to respond.
The distance of 10-15 feet between the truck and maruti car was certainly not a safe distance for which the driver of the maruti car must take the blame.
It must necessarily follow that the finding on the issue under consideration ought to be against the claimants.
19. In the above decision, the driver of the truck suddenly applied the break while the truck was in the centre of the road, bringing it to the right side, as a result of which, the Maruti car colluded with the truck from the back, due to which accident occurred, but in the present case, while overtaking the motor cycle, driver of the Swift car dashed to the petitioner's motor cycle, due to which accident occurred.
(SCCH-9) 22 MVC.No.7276/2023 20.
Further respondent No.1 has taken defence that petitioner was not wearing helmet at the time of alleged accident.
Petitioner was riding his two wheeler in zigzag manner and he himself has fell from the two wheeler and sustained injuries.
Hence, mere defence taken in the written statement is not sufficient to prove the same in the absence of documentary evidence.
The principle of "just compensation" requires that while contributory negligence can be a factor in determining the amount of compensation, it should not result in an unjust reduction.
The compensation must be fair and reasonable, reflecting the actual losses and the nature of injuries sustained.
By considering the above said citation, at the present case also, not wearing protective headgear does not negate the right to compensation.
